nodes.rationale: Define reusable VAD, STT, LLM, and TTS blocks, connect them into named pipelines. Unlike the CLI, YAML does not pick backends by platform, so backends must be named explicitly.

nodes.label: OpenAI-compatible STT Backend
nodes.rationale: Keeps VAD, turns, sessions, conversation state, and response handling inside speech-to-speech while delegating recognition to an external server via POST /v1/audio/transcriptions.

nodes.label: OpenAI Realtime Transcription (stateful streaming STT)
nodes.rationale: Sends incremental PCM over a persistent WebSocket with intent=transcription; local VAD still controls which audio is sent and when an utterance is committed.

nodes.label: OpenAI-compatible TTS Backend
nodes.rationale: Keeps turns, sessions, conversation state, and response handling inside speech-to-speech while delegating synthesis to an external server: LLM text -> POST /v1/audio/speech -> PCM16 at 16 kHz.

nodes.label: Response Latency Logs
nodes.rationale: Stages overlap and are not an additive breakdown; metadata version 2 moves e2e_s from VAD handoff to estimated speech end to first generated audio.

nodes.label: Big Bench Audio System Tests (vibe checks)
nodes.norm_label: big bench audio system tests (vibe checks)
nodes.rationale: Pinned Big Bench Audio recordings run through the engine's Realtime WebSocket API, exercising VAD, STT, LLM, and TTS with a fresh session per question.

nodes.label: Gemma 4 12B Native Audio Example (macOS)
nodes.rationale: Bypasses STT (--stt none) and forwards captured WAV directly to Gemma through llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint, so turn revisions, cancellation, and barge-in use the same Realtime path as other clients.

nodes.label: Streaming Diarization (Nemotron 3)
nodes.rationale: Diarization runs in a background worker on VAD-selected speech chunks; STT does not wait for it and late results never change an answer already started.

nodes.label: CancelScope
nodes.rationale: Replaces the old two-signal pattern (cancel_response Event + discard_stale_output boolean) with one object managing a generation counter and discard flag, so handlers can abort early on stale generations without timing games.

nodes.label: OpenAI Realtime Engine
nodes.rationale: Models run locally by default; the OpenAI Realtime protocol is only the client interface, served over WebSocket and WebRTC by a FastAPI/uvicorn server.

nodes.label: Speech-to-Visemes Stage (STV)
nodes.rationale: The stage is absent by default so disabling visemes requires no additional model download, memory, warmup, or buffering; extraction failures log and preserve audio playback and completion.

nodes.label: Progressive Audio Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Snapshots are emitted after each interval of accepted speech without splitting speech or ending the turn; consumers must handle changed audio rather than assume an exact final prefix.

nodes.label: Silero VAD Backend
nodes.rationale: Silero remains the default because streaming FireRedVAD has no published benchmark yet.

nodes.label: Voice Sales Agent (product architecture)
nodes.rationale: Architecture: Caller/Website over websocket -> VAD -> listening (STT) -> brain (LLM) -> voice (TTS); after the call: extract lead -> SQLite -> email (SMTP, Resend, or n8n; first that works).

nodes.label: Bounded Long Turns (STT)
nodes.rationale: openai_stt_max_window_s limits every transcription upload so requests stay under server duration/upload limits; completed text is reused across reopened speech and internal cuts do not trigger an assistant response.

nodes.label: Playback Buffering
nodes.rationale: A startup buffer absorbs early HTTP delivery jitter from remote TTS (196 ms default for local --tts openai) instead of stuttering; 0 ms for local backends keeps latency minimal.
